choices.text: United ORD-CMH nonstop: Tuesday 9:50 AM-12:00 PM; Friday 2:35 PM-2:55 PM; $336.
American ORD-CMH nonstop: Tuesday 10:35 AM-12:45 PM; Friday 12:50 PM-1:10 PM; $317.
Delta ORD-CMH nonstop: Tuesday 8:25 AM-10:35 AM; Friday 12:30 PM-12:50 PM; $324.
Southwest MDW-CMH nonstop: Tuesday 11:00 AM-1:10 PM; Friday 2:50 PM-3:10 PM; $329.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: the item neutralizes feasibility and uses only small fare differences. It requires combining the scoped soft United preference with the separate afternoon-return preference, while recognizing that United need only break a close comparison rather than override a meaningful disadvantage.
probes.gold_action: Put the United ORD-CMH itinerary first, with the Southwest MDW-CMH option retained as the close alternate.
probes.label_rationale: Every option reaches the Tuesday visit and has a return that is operationally workable, so the query does not establish a generic winner. The cheaper American and Delta choices trade their savings for noon-ish returns, which conflicts with Marisol's return-afternoon default. A and D then remain closely matched on ordinary utility: their fares differ by only $7 and both return in the afternoon. In this ordinary Chicago work-trip scope, United's positive but nonexclusive ranking weight makes A the appropriate lead rather than a forced rule; D remains a credible backup.
probes.query: Marisol is choosing one airfare hold from Chicago for a solo Columbus grant-site visit. Tuesday's host visit begins at 4:00 PM. Friday's debrief ends at 9:45 AM; the venue is 15 minutes from CMH, and the organizer has confirmed that each listed return works with its ground-transfer plan. All options have comparable standard-economy terms and carry-on allowance. No carrier has been requested for this trip. Which itinerary should be placed first on the hold list?

choices.text: United ORD-DTW nonstop: Tuesday 9:40 AM-11:55 AM; Thursday 2:35 PM-2:55 PM; $294. Hampton hotel total: $376, free breakfast, with several restaurants one block away. Whole package: $670.
Delta ORD-DTW nonstop: Tuesday 10:30 AM-12:45 PM; Thursday 2:50 PM-3:10 PM; $277. Courtyard hotel total: $372, no breakfast, with an on-site bistro. Whole package: $649.

American ORD-DTW nonstop: Tuesday 8:30 AM-10:45 AM; Thursday 12:40 PM-1:00 PM; $283. Fairfield hotel total: $368, free breakfast, with the nearest dinner restaurant a 10-minute walk away. Whole package: $651.

American ORD-DTW nonstop: Tuesday 11:20 AM-1:35 PM; Thursday 3:45 PM-4:05 PM; $270. Hyatt Place hotel total: $390, free breakfast, with the nearest dinner restaurant 0.7 miles away. Whole package: $660.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: resolving the package requires integrating the soft carrier preference with competing hotel-service, dining-access, and return-time preferences. The query supplies no user-specific value for breakfast, easy dinner access, airport choice, or an afternoon return, so a generic price-only ranking is not justified.
probes.gold_action: Lead with package A, the United-and-Hampton combination, and keep D as the lower-cost alternative if its less convenient dinner access is acceptable.
probes.label_rationale: The package totals intentionally leave no universal best choice. B is $21 cheaper and has on-site dinner but omits breakfast; C is cheaper with breakfast but has a pre-afternoon return; D is $10 cheaper with breakfast and an afternoon return but makes dinner access less convenient without a car. A combines the small, otherwise comparable United preference with included breakfast for early starts, nearby dining, and an afternoon return. Its $10-$21 premium is not a material generic disadvantage for that combined set of recurring preferences.
probes.query: Marisol is selecting a two-night Chicago-to-Detroit flight-and-hotel package for a solo grant-site visit. Wednesday and Thursday site meetings begin at 8:00 AM, and Thursday's closing discussion ends at 10:00 AM; the travel coordinator has confirmed that every listed return is feasible. She will not rent a car, and each refundable hotel is a seven-minute rideshare from the site with one queen bed, a coffee maker, and a refrigerator. Flight prices are standard main-cabin fares with carry-on only. Which package should lead the shortlist?

choices.text: United ORD-TPA nonstop: Tuesday 9:20 AM-12:55 PM; Thursday 5:25 PM-7:10 PM; $326.
Delta ORD-TPA nonstop: Tuesday 10:10 AM-1:45 PM; Thursday 2:35 PM-4:20 PM; $343.
American ORD-TPA nonstop: Tuesday 8:20 AM-11:55 AM; Thursday 12:50 PM-2:35 PM; $312.
Southwest MDW-TPA nonstop: Tuesday 10:40 AM-2:15 PM; Thursday 3:20 PM-5:10 PM; $351.

probes.difficulty_rationale: Hard: A and B are both fully viable nonstop choices with a small fare tradeoff, so the query alone cannot determine whether earlier return or lower price matters more. Correct resolution requires applying United as a soft preference and then allowing the stronger afternoon-return preference to override it when the United timing is substantially less attractive.
probes.gold_action: Use the Delta ORD-TPA itinerary as the working recommendation; retain the cheaper United option only as the budget backup.
probes.label_rationale: This tests the boundary on the United preference rather than treating it as exclusive. A saves only $17 but moves the return to an evening departure. B costs slightly more yet provides the recurring preferred afternoon return. C is cheaper but similarly gives up the afternoon return, while D also returns in the afternoon but costs more and uses Midway. Because return timing is the stronger recurring consideration, United's secondary positive weight should not force A when B offers the materially better return timing at a modest premium.
probes.query: Marisol is holding airfare from Chicago for a Tampa board convening. Tuesday's welcome begins at 5:00 PM. Thursday's final session ends at 10:35 AM; the hotel is 20 minutes from TPA, and the coordinator has verified that every listed return fits the official transfer plan. She will use rideshares, travel carry-on only, and book standard economy/main cabin. No carrier instruction applies to this trip. Which flight should be the working recommendation?
